note: Services and hours come from the partner SOW tool catalog. Hours are planning estimates, not a quote. Every service is grounded in the Adobe page named as its source.

starting_services.name: Forms onboarding, project setup and access
starting_services.scope: Enable the Forms solution on your client's Cloud Manager program (Forms - Digital Enrollment, plus the Communications add-on where documents are generated), run the build pipeline, add users to the Forms groups on Author and Publish, and set up the local SDK and the Archetype project developers deploy from.

adobe_source.title: Experience League: Onboard to AEM Forms as a Cloud Service

starting_services.name: Form templates, themes and fragments
starting_services.scope: Build the Adaptive Form templates, the theme that carries your client's brand and the reusable fragments (such as name and address panels) that every form starts from, on Core Components.

adobe_source.title: Experience League: Build an Adaptive Form template with Core Components

starting_services.name: Adaptive form build with rules
starting_services.scope: Build your client's first adaptive forms on Core Components (as a guide, one long multi-step application or about five short forms): panels and steps, fields, validation, and the rules that show, hide, calculate and call services.

adobe_source.title: Experience League: Form builder: Create forms with core components

starting_services.name: Form Data Model for back-end systems
starting_services.scope: Configure your client's data sources (REST, SOAP or OData services, or a relational database) and build the Form Data Model that prefills forms from the case or records system and writes submitted data back to it.

adobe_source.title: Experience League: Connect AEM Forms to a database

starting_services.name: Submit actions and server-side validation
starting_services.scope: Set each form's submit action (REST endpoint, Form Data Model, email, SharePoint, Azure Blob Storage or an AEM workflow) so data lands in a store your client owns, add a custom submit action where needed, and turn on server-side revalidation.

adobe_source.title: Experience League: Submit Actions Supported by Adaptive Forms

starting_services.name: Submission PDF for each form
starting_services.scope: Set up the Submission PDF (Document of Record) that keeps a print-friendly record of each submitted form: auto-generated, or on a branded XDP template built in Forms Designer and bound to the form's fields.

adobe_source.title: Experience League: Generate a Submission PDF (Document of Record) for Adaptive Forms (Core Components)

starting_services.name: Training for authors, developers and administrators
starting_services.scope: Train your client's team by role: form practitioners on building, styling and publishing forms, developers on custom components, workflows and the local SDK, and administrators on users, groups, data sources and configurations, with a handover guide.

adobe_source.title: Experience League: Onboard to AEM Forms as a Cloud Service

starting_services.name: Monthly forms releases and support
starting_services.scope: Publish your client's form and template changes each month, ship code through the Cloud Manager pipeline, check submissions and logs for errors, and republish forms whose cached images or fragments changed.

adobe_source.title: Experience League: Manage Publication in Experience Manager Forms

optional_services.name: Review and approval workflows
optional_services.scope: Build the AEM Workflow models that start when a form is submitted: assign review tasks to people or groups in the AEM Inbox, route approvals and rejections, send email notifications, and keep sensitive workflow data in your client's own storage.

adobe_source.title: Experience League: Use Forms-centric AEM Workflows - Step Reference to automate business processes

optional_services.name: E-signature with Acrobat Sign
optional_services.scope: Create the Acrobat Sign API application and the Acrobat Sign cloud configuration on Author and Publish, then add signing to your client's process with the Sign Document workflow step: the signers, the signing order and the signed document.

adobe_source.title: Experience League: Connect AEM Forms as a Cloud Service with Adobe Acrobat Sign

optional_services.name: Form analytics with Adobe Analytics
optional_services.scope: Set up a Tags property with the Adobe Experience Manager Forms and Adobe Analytics extensions, the data elements and rules for form events and the report suite mapping, then build your client's report on renders, submissions, errors and abandonment.

adobe_source.title: Experience League: Form Analytics with Adobe Analytics and AEM Forms - Complete Guide

optional_services.name: PDF form conversion to adaptive forms
optional_services.scope: Connect the Automated Forms Conversion service, convert your client's existing PDF forms (AcroForms, XFA-based or non-interactive) in batches within the service's size limits, then review and correct each converted form and apply your client's template and theme. The service produces forms on Foundation Components, the earlier of Adobe's two component sets for adaptive forms, so converted forms are maintained with that set's editor.

adobe_source.title: Experience League: Convert PDF forms to adaptive forms

optional_services.name: Migration from AEM 6.5 Forms
optional_services.scope: Move your client's forms from AEM 6.5 Forms on OSGi: run the Best Practices Analyzer, make forms, themes, templates and cloud configurations compatible with the Migration Utility on a cloned environment, then transfer them with the Content Transfer Tool.

adobe_source.title: Experience League: Migrate from AEM Forms (On-Premise and AMS environments) to AEM Forms as a Cloud Service

optional_services.name: Form accessibility review
optional_services.scope: Review your client's forms against the accessibility standard your client names, such as WCAG or Section 508, using the checks Adobe lists for form authors: an accessible name and description on every control, proper labels, text equivalents for images, sufficient color contrast and keyboard access. Test each form with an accessibility inspection tool, correct what the form's settings and theme control, and report what needs custom development.

adobe_source.title: Experience League: Creating accessible Adaptive Forms

optional_services.name: Document templates in Forms Designer
optional_services.scope: Create your client's letter, notice and document templates as XDP form designs in Forms Designer, define the XML data each one merges, and upload them to the Forms instance, including templates that replace a legacy system's output.

adobe_source.title: Experience League: AEM Forms as a Cloud Service Communication APIs

optional_services.name: On-demand document generation
optional_services.scope: Set up server-to-server credentials and connect your client's application to the synchronous Communications APIs, so a letter or PDF is generated from a template and data the moment a form is submitted or a case worker asks for it.

adobe_source.title: Experience League: AEM Forms as a Cloud Service Communication APIs

optional_services.name: Batch document generation
optional_services.scope: Connect your client's Microsoft Azure Storage, create the batch data store and the batch configurations, and set up the scheduled runs from your client's application that turn a set of records into PDF or print documents.

adobe_source.title: Experience League: AEM Forms as a Cloud Service Communications Batch Processing

optional_services.name: PDF/A output and document assembly
optional_services.scope: Add the document steps your client's records policy needs: convert generated PDFs to PDF/A and validate them, and assemble or split document packages with DDX, including the Dispatcher rule those APIs need.

adobe_source.title: Experience League: AEM Forms as a Cloud Service Communication APIs

starting_services.name: Account, users, groups and sign-in
starting_services.scope: Set up your client's account structure: groups for each business unit with their own settings, branding and templates, account and group administrators, users and their report access, and sign-in through the Adobe Admin Console with single sign-on.

adobe_source.title: Adobe Help: Manage Groups in Adobe Acrobat Sign

starting_services.name: Account settings, branding and security
starting_services.scope: Configure the account and group settings your client's policies call for: company name, logo and email branding, signature preferences, send settings, security settings and the external archive that receives a copy of every signed agreement.

adobe_source.title: Adobe Help: Set up your Acrobat Sign company account

starting_services.name: Library templates and form fields
starting_services.scope: Turn your client's most used agreements into library templates with signature, date and data fields for each signer, built in the authoring environment or with text tags, and set who may use and edit each one.

adobe_source.title: Adobe Help: Create a library template (Acrobat Sign)

starting_services.name: Custom send workflows
starting_services.scope: Build workflow templates in the Custom Workflow Designer for your client's regular agreement types: recipients and routing, the documents and fields included, email copies, expiration and passwords, with instructions for senders.

adobe_source.title: Adobe Help: Custom Workflow Designer overview (Acrobat Sign)

starting_services.name: Training for senders, template authors and administrators
starting_services.scope: Train your client's team by role: senders on sending, tracking and reminders, template authors on fields, templates and workflows, administrators on users, groups, settings and reports, with a handover guide.

adobe_source.title: Experience League: Acrobat Sign tutorials, administrators overview

starting_services.name: Monthly agreement reporting and template upkeep
starting_services.scope: Each month, run agreement reports on completion rates and time to sign, review which templates and workflows stall, update templates and settings, and manage users and groups.

adobe_source.title: Adobe Help: Agreement reports (Acrobat Sign)

optional_services.name: Web forms on your client's site
optional_services.scope: Create signable web forms for agreements people start themselves, with participants, counter-signers and signer authentication, and embed them on your client's website or share them as links.

adobe_source.title: Adobe Help: Create a web form (Acrobat Sign)

optional_services.name: Bulk sending from a recipient list
optional_services.scope: Set up Send in Bulk for agreements that go to many people at once: the parent template, the CSV file with recipients and merge fields, and how your client's team tracks the agreements it creates.

adobe_source.title: Adobe Help: Overview of Send in Bulk (Acrobat Sign)

optional_services.name: Signer identity checks and digital signatures
optional_services.scope: Choose the identity check for each kind of agreement your client sends, such as Acrobat Sign authentication, a phone or knowledge-based check or a provider on the Digital Identity Gateway, set the defaults by group, and enable digital signatures where the law or your client's policy asks for them.

adobe_source.title: Adobe Help: Acrobat Sign Digital Identity Gateway

optional_services.name: Retention rules and audit records
optional_services.scope: Set data governance rules that delete agreements and their data after the retention period your client's records policy sets, and agree where signed copies and audit reports are kept before they are deleted.

adobe_source.title: Adobe Help: Data governance overview (Acrobat Sign)

optional_services.name: API and webhook integration with your client's systems
optional_services.scope: Connect your client's application to the Acrobat Sign REST API: the API application and OAuth, agreements sent from templates with your client's data, and webhooks that tell your client's system when an agreement is signed, so signed documents and field data return to it.

adobe_source.title: Adobe Help: Acrobat Sign webhooks overview

optional_services.name: Acrobat Sign for Salesforce
optional_services.scope: Install and configure the Acrobat Sign for Salesforce package in your client's Salesforce org: permission sets, agreement templates with data mappings and merge fields, and buttons that send for signature from a record.

adobe_source.title: Adobe Help: Acrobat Sign for Salesforce installation guide

optional_services.name: Acrobat Sign for Microsoft 365 and Teams
optional_services.scope: Deploy the Acrobat Sign add-ins for Teams, Outlook, Word and PowerPoint from the Microsoft admin center, connect them to your client's Acrobat Sign account, and show teams how to send and track agreements from the apps they work in.

adobe_source.title: Adobe Help: Adobe Acrobat Sign for Microsoft 365

optional_services.name: Acrobat Sign for Workday
optional_services.scope: Connect Acrobat Sign to your client's Workday tenant: the OAuth relationship, the business process steps that send documents for signature, and a service account for the Workday group.

adobe_source.title: Adobe Help: Adobe Acrobat Sign for Workday installation guide

starting_services.name: Cloud Manager program, pipelines and access
starting_services.scope: Assign AEM product profiles in the Admin Console, create the production program and environments in Cloud Manager, set up Git access and the first deployment pipelines.

adobe_source.title: Experience League: AEM as a Cloud Service Onboarding Journey Introduction

starting_services.name: Site build with components and templates
starting_services.scope: Build the site from the AEM Project Archetype or a Site Template, with Core Components, editable templates, client-side libraries and the custom components the design needs.

adobe_source.title: Experience League: Get started with AEM Sites - WKND tutorial

starting_services.name: Go-live checklist and cutover
starting_services.scope: Work through Adobe's go-live checklist: a production pipeline with functional and UI tests, Dispatcher validation, CDN, SSL and DNS, performance and security tests on stage, notification profiles and traffic filter rules.

adobe_source.title: Experience League: Go-Live Checklist

starting_services.name: Author training on the Universal Editor
starting_services.scope: Train authors to edit pages and content in the Universal Editor and hand over authoring guides for the site's components and templates.

adobe_source.title: Experience League: Universal Editor Introduction

starting_services.name: Monthly releases, monitoring and logs
starting_services.scope: Each month, ship code through Cloud Manager pipelines, check the automatic AEM version updates, review logs and the Developer Console, and fix issues found after go-live.

adobe_source.title: Experience League: Post Go-Live

optional_services.name: Content migration with Content Transfer Tool
optional_services.scope: Where your client is moving from AEM on-premise or Adobe Managed Services: extract and ingest content with the Content Transfer Tool in Cloud Acceleration Manager, then run differential top-ups before go-live.

adobe_source.title: Experience League: Overview to Content Transfer Tool

connections.what: Adaptive forms are built in, or placed on, AEM Sites pages; the Forms Portal lists forms, drafts and submissions there
connections.how: AEM Forms provides the Adaptive Forms Container and Adaptive Forms Embed components, so your authors create a form inside an AEM Sites page or Experience Fragment, or place an existing form there. The Forms Portal components list forms, saved drafts and submissions on your Sites pages.
needs_first: Adaptive Forms Core Components: forms in the Page Editor use them
The Adaptive Forms client libraries added to the site's page components through the deployment pipeline (a code change)
The Adaptive Forms Container allowed in the policy of the page templates
Forms placed with the Embed component do not get Sites versioning, targeting, translation or multi-site management
For drafts and submissions in the Forms Portal: your client's Azure Storage account and access key, connected through the Unified Storage Connector
Signed-in users for the portal: only logged-in users can edit drafts or see what they submitted
For one theme across site and forms: the front-end pipeline configured for the site theme

services.name: Adaptive forms on AEM Sites pages
services.scope: Add the Adaptive Forms client libraries to the site's page components through the deployment pipeline, allow the Adaptive Forms Container in the page templates, and build or embed the first forms on pages and Experience Fragments.

adobe_source.title: Experience League: Add an Adaptive Form to an AEM Sites page or Experience Fragment

services.name: Forms Portal with drafts and submissions
services.scope: Build the forms portal on site pages with the Search & Lister, Drafts & Submissions and Link components, connect your client's Azure Storage through the Unified Storage Connector, and confirm site sign-in, since only signed-in people can resume drafts and see their submissions.

adobe_source.title: Experience League: Introduction to Forms Portal

services.name: One theme for site and forms
services.scope: Embed the Adaptive Forms theme in the AEM Sites theme so one build and one front-end pipeline deployment styles both the pages and the forms on them.

adobe_source.title: Experience League: Embed an Adaptive Forms theme in an AEM Sites theme

connections.what: Acrobat Sign cloud configuration in AEM Forms sends form documents for signature, from a workflow step or a sign-enabled form
connections.how: Your forms in AEM Forms send the completed document to Acrobat Sign. Your signers receive it by email and sign in the order you set, and the signed copy and its status return to your process.
needs_first: An active Acrobat Sign developer account and an Acrobat Sign API application, for its Client ID and Client Secret
The cloud configuration pointed at the Acrobat Sign shard the account lives on
For forms on Core Components: signing through the Sign Document workflow step, since signing inside the form is not supported
An email address for every signer
For Government ID checks: that authentication method enabled in Acrobat Sign

services.name: Signing on forms built with Foundation Components
services.scope: Enable Acrobat Sign on your client's Foundation Components forms, such as forms produced by the Automated Forms Conversion service: the signers and their order, signer authentication, the Acrobat Sign fields placed in the document, and the document each signer receives.

adobe_source.title: Experience League: Use Adobe Sign in an Adaptive Form

adobe_facts.fact: There are two documented routes. The simpler one: forms built in Marketo Engage are embedded on the site's pages with Marketo's own embed code, so each submission is a Marketo form fill. We would place the embed in a reusable page component, agree the fields, consent wording and validation with you, and collect only the data you approve. Marketo's form prefill does not work with the embed code.

adobe_facts.fact: The fuller one: AEM Forms adaptive forms with the Submit to Marketo Engage action, which add a rule editor, prefill and a PDF record of each submission, and can connect to Adobe Sign for e-signatures. We would use embedded Marketo forms for standard lead capture and adaptive forms where a form needs that logic.
